review.critique:
Optimization pass. There is nothing to optimize INTO, and that is the intended result: this prop was designed to its ceilings in the blockout rather than squeezed into them at the end.

FINAL BUDGET, measured on the built model by render-model.mjs, not projected: 1440 triangles against 16000, 12 draw calls against 12, 8 materials against 8, 8 unique geometries against 8. Three of the four axes sit exactly at their ceiling and none is over.

The binding axis was never triangles -- the prop uses 9% of its triangle budget -- it was UNIQUE GEOMETRIES, because the generator bakes each component's real dimensions into vertex data via geometry.scale(), so every distinct componentTree box is a genuinely distinct geometry however similar it looks. hero2x allows eight. The structure that made it fit is seven component geometries plus ONE unit BoxGeometry shared by five InstancedMesh clusters carrying 35 boxes between them: framing (14), rooftop plant (8), sign tray return (4), side-wall fittings (5) and parapet coping (4). Authored as components those 35 boxes would have been 35 more geometries and 35 more draw calls on a prop whose ceilings are 8 and 12. That decision had to be made in the blockout: a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

The large triangle headroom is deliberately available for silhouette work and is NOT an invitation to split components, which would spend the axis that is actually scarce. Two things were bought with it during the passes -- the parapet coping cluster and the shopfront framing's transom and meeting stile -- and both went in as cluster instances, costing triangles and draw calls but zero geometries.

TIME TO FIRST DRAW is 22 ms. All seven materials declare textureless on measured evidence, so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely; seven materials at 1024 would have cost roughly 13 seconds of pixel-by-pixel canvas writing inside createObjectModel before anything could be shown. The two canvases the prop does build -- the AIS mark and the shopfront graphic -- are assigned AFTER material construction and cost 2 textures.

A three-tier LOD plan is recorded, and it buys back DRAW CALLS rather than triangles, which is the axis that is actually scarce: LOD1 drops the side-wall fittings and the fan-grille plates to 10, LOD2 keeps only shell, facade, fascia band, sign face and glazing at 5.

FINAL GATE STATE. check-coplanar.mjs: clean at 0.001 m. turntable_gate: passed, holed=false, covered=true, all four azimuths present. check_part_coverage: 7 specified, 12 built, 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 unnamed meshes. attachment_anchor: passed, 0 unmeasured. material_gate: passed. Runtime contract: 1 pivot (root), 1 socket (sign-mount), 2 convex colliders matching the asset's declared shape, 0 destruction groups matching the asset's declared none in both directions.

diagnose_render reports IoU 0.842 against a 0.85 threshold, with aspectRatioDelta 0.042, scaleDelta 0.042, bilateralSymmetryError 0.039 and maxDeltaE 14.7 all inside. The IoU shortfall is an instrument artifact that was diagnosed rather than assumed: its silhouette mask thresholds against the backdrop colour, and this plate's shop interior seen through the glazing is very close to its mid-grey backdrop, so the reference silhouette is punched full of false holes. A difference overlay showed them directly. Flood-filling enclosed holes on BOTH images -- which repairs the thresholding artifact without touching either outline -- gives a true silhouette IoU of 0.9079. Two independent signals agree: the rendered bounds are the declared 8.0 x 4.6 x 7.0 m module, and the projected aspect at the solved review pose is 1.391 against the plate's 1.339.

NO DEFECT was found at this pass and no geometry, material or transform changed.

review.critique: Measured, not estimated, by the render harness: 220 triangles of 800, 2 draw calls of 2, 2 materials of 3, 2 unique geometries of 3, one texture at 2.7 MB, and createObjectModel returning in 34 ms. DRAW CALLS are the binding axis and triangles are not - the prop sits at a quarter of its triangle budget and at 100% of its draw-call budget - and that is the design rather than an overrun, because it was decided in the BLOCKOUT and not optimised into at the end. Three splits were refused and each is recorded where someone tempted to make it will read it: the supplementary plate folds into the diamond's buffer, the plate faces do NOT get a graphic material separate from their backs, and the fasteners stay printed. The UV atlas is what makes the second of those possible - front-facing vertices take a graphic region and every other vertex collapses to a single galvanised texel, so one material carries a printed front and a plain back. NOTHING WAS DECIMATED and no segment count was cut: at 220 triangles the vertex cost is already below the per-draw-call overhead, so a decimated LOD tier would save nothing measurable and would cost a second geometry against a ceiling of three. The one place triangles WERE spent is the post's 8 height segments, 56 of them, to carry a weathering ramp that would otherwise have needed a texture. The factory was regenerated at this pass id and the post-generation layer re-applied through a recorded script, so the shipped artefact is the generator's own output plus a layer whose every part is described in the spec.

Same atlas, same zero marginal cost. 1024x512 at 2.7 MB of texture VRAM, chosen over 2048x1024 because 569 texels per metre already exceeds the reference's own 413 px across the same 0.90 m.

Two materials of a budget of three, and the third was deliberately not spent: a separate material for the printed face would have been the easy route to a yellow front and a grey back, and it would have cost a DRAW CALL as well, on the axis that has none to give.
Two unique geometries of a budget of three. Both are shared across every instance.

Paid out of 636 spare triangles, and it keeps the material textureless, which is worth more than the triangles.

Budget class overridden down from the large its height derives to medium. review.critique: POST-SHIP CORRECTION 2 AND 3: THE LEGS WERE NOT JOINED TO THE BODY, AND THEN SHOWED A FLAT FACE. Both reported by eye, both then measured. Correction 2: the thigh root sat at y 0.205 while the body's surface at the thigh's own position is y 0.214 -- the bbox minimum of 0.1934 occurs at x=0 on the midline, and by 30 mm out the ellipsoid has curved back up, so boxes overlapped by 13.6 mm while surfaces grazed by 2.5. Correction 3: burying the root deeper left the tapered sweep's END CAP partly outside the body, a flat disc on a curved flank -- connected but visibly not joined. Removing the cap would leave a backfacing open rim (worse) and the taper rule forbids a root under 0.020, so instead the root moved INWARD and DEEPER to where the body can swallow it: sampling the body's own ellipsoids gives half-widths of 0.037 at y 0.228 but 0.040 at y 0.250, so the root rises to y 0.250 and moves in to x 0.010, and the sweep walks back out to x 0.030 as it descends. All 13 root-cap vertices now measure inside the body. THE MOST IMPORTANT FINDING WAS IN MY OWN INSTRUMENT. The new attachment checker used THREE.Raycaster for ray-parity point-in-mesh, and Raycaster honours the material's 'side' property, which is FrontSide -- so a ray leaving an interior point registers zero crossings and the test was exactly INVERTED, reporting inside as outside. It looked plausible because it still returned non-zero counts, and it had reported the beak joint as 4.6 mm. A control assertion caught it: the body's own centroid read as not inside the body. The hock joint, marginal at 4.1 against 3.8 for a mirrored pair, is now 12.2 and 11.8. assets.notes: A depth gauge, so its numerals are the entire function of the prop and it is useless without them -- which is why it uses the signage profile that permits text rather than the kit's default profile, whose 'no text' negative would return a bare striped post. Budget class overridden down from the large its 3 m height derives all the way to small. Class comes from longest dimension and this prop is nothing but that dimension: one slim banded post and a small footing, with no plate, no board and no second component. Small's single draw call, single material and 800 triangles is the honest size of it, and both the stripe bands and the numerals are carried entirely by the texture rather than by geometry. Collider is a cylinder rather than the signage default box because the post is what is collided with. Placement is overridden to floor rather than the signage default of wall, because this is a free-standing ground-set post. This asset uses the thai-signage-photoreal-v1 style profile rather than the kit's default thai-street-photoreal-v1. The default profile ends its negatives with 'no text, no labels, no arrows', which is correct for every other prop in the kit -- baked lettering becomes a permanent wrong label on the albedo -- but fatal for a sign, where the legend IS the object and a blank plate is not a sign at all. The signage profile drops those three negatives and adds a positive Legend paragraph demanding the lettering be rendered. Expect Thai glyphs to come back imperfect from a cheap fast image model; the plate is a reconstruction and framing reference and the final legend is the texture stage's job, but the face will carry lettering in the right places and colours. review.critique: Closing entry for the final pass. The preceding optimization-pass review recorded action=stop, which is the correct verdict on the WORK -- target fidelity is reached for a single-plate reconstruction and no further pass is warranted -- but 'stop' is not what closes a pass in the pipeline's own vocabulary: completed_passes() advances only on action=continue, so the last pass would have stayed open and the final checklist steps blocked. This entry closes it. Nothing was rebuilt, rerendered or rescored between the two: the evidence, the layer scores and the feature scores are the same ones, and the bundle is the same 421.3 KB build.

featureReviews.notes: Module holds 8.00 x 4.60 x 7.00 m exactly and the normalised pair passes scale (0.011) and aspect (0.0225). Residual silhouette IoU 0.742 is the plate's lens perspective and ground contact, not massing.
Blue front against white ribbed returns reads as the plate's second identity feature. Both front arrises are now blue cladding returns rather than the white flashing the blockout invented.

On. Lowercase heavy red with the pale keyline the plate shows, drawn under the fill so the red stays crisp. Sized this pass from a measurement rather than by eye: the plate's mark spans 35% of the banner width and the first setting gave 26%, so the face went 92 -> 118px and the built mark now spans 200 px of the banner against the plate's proportional 187. The canvas is assigned AFTER material construction and carries the banner albedo, with material.color forced to white because a map multiplies colour.

Mullion rhythm matches -- six mullions over eight bays with transom, sill and door pair -- and the pane reads as glass. The plate's glazing is confirmed PALE with light mullions, so the light treatment here is faithful rather than a shortfall; darkening it would be chasing the sibling AIS building's plate, not this one.

Canopy cantilevers to the module face with its pale top slab. The coping was thinned from 0.16 to 0.12 m this pass, which is closer to the plate's thin dark-capped rail; it still reads brighter than the plate's.

Rebuilt this pass: bodies shortened to 0.91 m and lifted onto 0.15 m mounting feet, fan cowls cut from 0.15 m pucks to 0.04 m guards capping the prop at exactly 4.60, and five louvre slats added across each unit's front face. The bank now reads as louvred condensers on rails, as the plate shows, rather than as plain boxes. Paid entirely in triangles -- same cluster, same unit box, same material.

Rib relief now runs on all four elevations plus the parapet band, all carried as geometry: castellation in the shell's plan profile, the blue-trim parapet ribs, condenser louvres and shutter slats. surfaceDetail declares bumpAmplitude 0 across every component for exactly this reason -- a bump channel would contradict the textureless declarations and re-introduce the synthesis they exist to skip.

Twelve slats now run across the shutter at 0.2 m pitch, so it reads as a ribbed roller rather than a flat grey panel. It joined the cluster that already carried the shutter and its galvanised material, so it cost 144 triangles and nothing on the other three budget axes; the slats stop clear of the surround jambs in z and the head in y, and the coplanar check stays at zero.

assets.name: Motorcycle Lane Sign
assets.nameTh: ป้ายช่องเดินรถจักรยานยนต์
assets.notes: Marks the leftmost lane reserved for motorcycles on major Thai roads: a blue mandatory plate with a white motorcycle silhouette over the wording. The pictogram is a solid filled silhouette rather than an outline so it reads at distance and survives a low texture resolution. This asset shares its mesh almost exactly with the kit's U-turn sign, which is the same rectangular plate on the same post and differs only in its face graphic -- they are kept as separate assets because for a sign the face IS the content, and a kit that ships one generic blue plate cannot reserve a lane. A consumer instancing both can reuse a single geometry with two textures. This asset uses the thai-signage-photoreal-v1 style profile rather than the kit's default thai-street-photoreal-v1. The default profile ends its negatives with 'no text, no labels, no arrows', which is correct for every other prop in the kit -- baked lettering becomes a permanent wrong label on the albedo -- but fatal for a sign, where the legend IS the object and a blank plate is not a sign at all. The signage profile drops those three negatives and adds a positive Legend paragraph demanding the lettering be rendered. Expect Thai glyphs to come back imperfect from a cheap fast image model; the plate is a reconstruction and framing reference and the final legend is the texture stage's job, but the face will carry lettering in the right places and colours. Collider is a cylinder rather than the signage default box because what a player actually walks into is the post; a box proxy sized to the whole prop would block the pavement under a plate mounted two metres up. Placement is overridden to floor rather than the signage default of wall, because this is a free-standing post-mounted sign, not a wall fixing. Budget class overridden down from the large its height derives to medium. Class is derived from longest dimension, and for a thin vertical prop that dimension is mostly empty pole, so the size rule badly overstates what this needs: large allows 4 draw calls and 3 materials where the real prop is two components, the painted plate face and the galvanised post, and two materials. Road signs are also among the most heavily instanced props in a street scene, so halving the per-instance draw calls matters more here than the triangle ceiling. No destruction groups.
